text: TROUBLE AT HANKOW.

label: text
text:
" Grave
Anti - Foreign

label: text
text: CUSTOMS WORKERS' UNION.

label: text
text: General Strike Makes Great Progress.

label: text
text: FEAR OF AN "INCIDENT."

label: text
text: The trouble at Hankow was raised in the House of Commons yesterday when the Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, replying to the Leader of the Opposition, dwept upon the gravity of the situation.

label: paragraph_title
text: Serious Developments.

label: text
text:
Rugby, Nov. 29.
Sir Austen Chamberlain, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, was questioned in the House of Commons by Mr. Ramsay MacDonald, Leader of the Opposition, regarding the condition of affairs at Hankow. He replied that serious developments in the situation had taken place there during the past week and a grave anti-foreign movement appeared to be at work.

label: paragraph_title
text: HANKOW TROUBLE.

label: paragraph_title
text:
American Warships
Move.

label: text
text: The Flotilla Leader Keppel went to Hankow this morning. The American destroyers "Peary" and "John D. Ford left yesterday. —Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: "Situation Essier."

label: text
text: The latest report was that the situation in some respects appeared to be easier. The union had presented its demands, and these were not expected to be of an impossible nature, though it might be that they were only a preliminary move.

label: text
text:
A union of the lower grade employees of the Chinese Maritime Customs was formed on November 21 with the support of the superintendent who was a Chinese official. This union had announced that its aim was to oust the foreign element from the management of the service and bring it under purely Chinese control.
The "Commissioner of Customs hoped it might be "possible" to keep the Customs House open and maintain the light service for foreign nations, but this might be difficult. The Customs House, which was in the Chinese City was picketed.

label: text
text: At the same time the general strike had made great progress. Chinese servants of Japanese were already on strike, and Japanese had had to import their food supplies from other centres.

label: text
text: The Communist section was showing great activity, and there was a fear of a general strike being forced. This, if carried out, would throw out of employment thousands of the lower grade workers, and it would be easy to incite these to riot. The situation was being watched by British Government.

label: text
text: In official circles in London it is pointed out that Hankow is easily defensible. Though it is 800 miles from the mouth of the Yangtse, the River at that point is a mile and a half wide, and comparatively large battleships can lie off the waterfront—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text:
Sir Austen Chamberlain, replying to a further question, said the Foreign Office had received a cable from the British community at Hankow stating that the situation was very grave indeed, that they were in daily expectation of an incident which would involve blood-shed, and that the naval forces were not adequate for protection of the community, and asking the Government to give an assurance that these forces would be strengthened. Sir Austen Chamberlain said that this appeal was under the consideration of the Government, including the Admiralty.
Situation

label: paragraph_title
text: Customs Position.

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, replying to Mr. Ramsay MacDonald, Leader of the Opposition, whose first appearance it was since his return from abroad, Sir Austen Chamberlain. Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, referred to the grave anti-foreign movement at Hankow, including the aims of the newly-formed union of the lower grade customs employees.

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain said that the Commissioner of Customs hoped to keep the "Customs House open and maintain the lights service with foreign labour, but this might be difficult if the Customs House were picketed.

label: text
text: The latest report showed that the situation in this respect was somewhat easier. The union had presented demands, but these were understood not to be of an impossible nature, though possibly this was only a preliminary move.

label: paragraph_title
text: Navali Forces.

label: text
text: Replying to Mr. H. W. Looken Sir Ausur Chamberlain said that a British request from Hankow for the strengthening for the naval forces there was being considered by the Government and Admiralty. —Reuter.

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain mentioned the latest facts about the progress of the general strike, movement and Communist activities. He hoped to afford Mr. Ramsay MacDonald information on December 1 if he would repeat his question.

label: text
text: [Mr. Herbert William Looker has been Unionist M.P. for Essex since 1924. He came to Hong Kong in 1895 to join the local firm of solicitors now known as Deacon's. "He was admitted a partner in 1900 and retired in 1919.]

label: paragraph_title
text: Views of "The Times."

label: text
text: The seriousness of the Cantonese advance in China is emphasised in a lender in the "Times" which says that it is a very serious and urgent matter to the foreign interests, especially British which are now very greatly endangered and for the British Government there is "at the present time in the international sphere no more urgent question. Measures, it says must be taken immediately to protect British nationals who are endangered on the Yangtze and it must clearly be longescen that the opportunities of provoking further conflict are innumerable and that the worse enemies of Britain are watching to take advantage of them.

label: paragraph_title
text: London, Nov. 29.

label: text
text: He adds that hesitation is a very dangerous policy for all, and that to trust vaguely in some ultimate Chinese reaction by anti-Bolsheviks is wholly unprofitable, for by the time the reaction comes there may be very little left for us to save and the state of China herself will be appalling.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: Naval Forces Being Landed.

label: text
text: Following threats of a general strike at Hankow against foreigners, the Shanghai Chinese General Chamber of Commerce has received anonymous threatening letters demanding that a strike be called here.

label: text
text: A message from Hankow of November 28 says shipping employees and the municipal policemen have threatened to strike unless certain demands be granted.

label: paragraph_title
text: Priest Captured.

label: text
text: Disbanded soldiers captured the Belgian Father Petecn last week in the bishopric of Sui-yuan, Shani.

label: text
text: The French Legation, which has always been responsible for the protection of Belgian missionaries, has protested to the Foreign Office, urging that measures be taken to obtain the Father's immediate release.

text: ST. ANDREW'S DAY.

text: Scottish Clans at Ball To-night.

Needless to say the interests of Scottish residents—and their friends — will be centred in the Ball and dinner at the City Hall to-night where the spirit of revelry will hold sway till the small hours of the morning.

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON SURPRISE.

label: paragraph_title
text: MILITARY ACTION AGAINST STRIKERS.

label: text
text: Chairman Arrested.

label: text
text: Much significance is attached to the arrest, by the highest military authority in Canton, of the chairman of the Executive of the Strike Committee and four other delegates who have all along had an active voice in the management of the boycott of Hong Kong.

label: text
text: On Sunday night, a detachment from the headquarters (in Canton) of the commander-in-chief (General Chang Kni-shek), was sent out to make the arrests.

label: text
text: Mr. Sp Shiu-ching is the Strike chairman, sitting on the Executive of delegates as the representative of the Seamen's Union.

label: text
text: In the 1922 shipping strike at Hong Kong, he was one of the leaders. Subsequently one of his colleagues fell into disgrace following a scandal, and the first general secretary of the Hong Kong Union seceded after a dispute which culminated in a stormy meeting in the Des Voeux Road headquarters, at which the Police were present.

label: text
text: Mr. So presided at that momentous meeting and since then" has been head of the Seamen, with offices at Canton.

label: paragraph_title
text: " Who the Chairman Is:

label: text
text: Earlier this year, some of the delegates who sat on the Strike tribunal were detained by the Nationalist Government but what happened to them is not definitely known.

label: text
text: When the Strike began last June, he became chairman of the Strike Executive, the highest position in the movement.

label: text
text: Mr. So was also the spokesman of the strikers when a delegation of Hong Kong Chinese merchants went up last year to explore the possibilities of a settlement.

label: paragraph_title
text: Speculation Rife

label: text
text: Three weeks ago, the Strike headquarters at East Garden, Canton, were destroyed by a fire. A committee of investigation reported that “enemies of the movement” had committed arson.

label: text
text: The present opinion is that, accusations were laid against the Strike Executive by two bodies. Formerly, it had been alleged that several millions of dollars had to be accounted for, and a semi-official announcement followed to the effect that an authoritative statement of accounts would be presented when ready.

label: text
text: Speculation is rife as to the motive behind the arrest of Mr. So. In the circumstances the Canton Government can hardly be expected to make a statement, at least until investigations are complete.

text: RUBBER CLAIM

label: text
text: COMMERCIAL POSSIBILITIES

label: text
text: Bogota, Colombia, Nov. 29.

label: text
text: According to a Riohacha message the Venezuelan consul, Rodriguez Arcia, after experimenting for fifteen years, has discovered a process for extracting rubber for commercial purposes from a new plant growing wild all over Colombia. The Minister of Industry has sent a commission to investigate.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE WEATHER.

label: text
text: At 11.22 a.m. to-day the Observatory reported:—Pressure has increased slightly at the majority of stations. The anticyclone has been absorbed by a larger one, central over S.E. Mongolia. Moderate monsoon may be expected along the S.E. coast of China and over the China Sea.

label: text
text: Till noon to-morrow the official weather forecast for all local districts is: -moderate E. winds cloudy!

label: text
text: Meteorological observations at 6 a.m. to day: barometer 29.99; temperature 60; humidity 89; wind E., force 8; weather overcast; airzale.

label: paragraph_title
text: Merchants' View.

label: text
text: The report, it is interesting to note, says that Mr. So and his four colleagues are under close detention at general headquarters.

label: text
text: Merchants, of course, regard this incident in the light of the Canton authorities making a definite move to curb boycott agitation, it having been announced that the Nationalist policy is to preserve communications.

label: text
text: This is only surmise and, in the light of developments in other directions, can only be treated as such.

label: paragraph_title
text: SEAMEN'S TROUBLE.

label: paragraph_title
text: Canton Government Not to Intervene?

label: text
text: Intimidation — it is called “peaceful picketting”—continues against intercourse with the Steamboat Co.'s vessels and wharves at Canton.

label: text
text: Other than providing armed police to preserve order generally at the wharves, steps have still to be taken to curb the activities of ex-seamen strikers, who are alleged to be sponsored by their Union.

label: text
text: The seamen want the dismissal of certain members of the crews in addition to their own reinstatement and a deadlock has been reached in the negotiations.

label: text
text: In Canton circles it is not expected that the authorities will take any action in the matter, pending other possibilities of an understanding.

label: paragraph_title
text: OTHER DIFFICULTIES.

label: paragraph_title
text: Problems for Nationalists to Solve.

label: text
text: Several other difficulties are engaging the attention of the Nationalist and the Canton (municipal) Governments.

label: text
text: The four Chambers of Commerce have petitioned the Municipality to take precautions to protect the public food supply, in view of the portents of the present general strike at rice shops.

label: text
text: The waterworks dispute is still outstanding.

label: text
text: In connection with the removal of the seat of Nationalist Government from Canton to Wuchang, a number of obstacles “behind the scenes” remain to be cleared.

label: text
text: One section of the officials are stated "to be not in favour—although not openly opposing—the drastic change. Their argument is that Kwangtung is the home of the Party and is still the most important province.

label: text
text:
Military Powers.
Gossip is also busy with the delay in the assumption by General Li Chai-sum of the post of head of the Military Department.

label: text
text: General Li is acting commander-in-chief of the Canton garrison, in the absence of General Chang Kai-shek. He is also the commander of the 4th Nationalist Army, two divisions of which (the 10th and 12th) have won the highest honours in the war.

label: text
text: The disposition of the Canton Navy is blamed for the delay. The present Commander of the Navy is reported to be reluctant to go under the control of General Li and he is said to have communicated with General Chang Kai-shek in the matter.

label: text
text: The creation of the new department of military affairs was approved by the last Kuomintang Conference in Canton.
